heading: Dijkstra needs more than just cost
body:
Regular Dijkstra tracks min cost per city — but here a **cheaper path** might violate the stop limit while a **pricier path** is valid.

**Fix**: Track `(cost, city, stops)` so the same city can be visited with different stop counts. Each `(city, stops)` pair = distinct state.

heading: When to extend Dijkstra's state
body:
Use `(cost, node, extra_dimension)` for:

- **Limited hops/stops**: `(cost, node, stops)`
- **Fuel constraints**: `(cost, node, fuel)`
- **Must-visit checkpoints**: `(cost, node, visited_mask)`
- **Time windows**: `(cost, node, arrival_time)`

If cost alone isn't enough → extend the state.

label: Crux · Python

q: Why does standard Dijkstra fail for this problem?
options: It cannot handle negative edge weights
It only tracks minimum cost per city, ignoring the stop constraint
It requires a complete graph to work correctly
explain: Standard Dijkstra tracks only one value per city (minimum cost) and marks it visited, missing valid but pricier paths that use fewer stops.
